name: Halftone Printing (Printmaking and Craft Materials; explicitly sourced direction).
visualIdentity: Tone comes from dot size or density, with consistent dot shape, spacing, and angle. Halftones pair with limited color separations, clear outlines, and paper texture. Dots stay anchored to the artwork during motion and are generated from source luminance.
suitableUses: Source-listed fits: product and editorial introductions, explanatory narratives, chaptered abstract motion, and tonal imagery as primary content. Source examples are editorial feature intros and comic-print product spins. Other suitability is unspecified.
limitations: Inspect scaling for moire and lost text detail, avoiding non-integer scaling and dot frequencies near the pixel grid. Never halftone text; use masks to protect text and emissive screens. The red accent fails body-text contrast (4.03:1), so keep it decorative. A simulated look is not proof of physical printing.
palette: Suggested, not supplied: paper #F8EFD9 background, dark blue #253E56 foreground, and red #C25143 accent. These are three discrete inks with gradients disabled. Foreground on paper reaches 9.64:1, while red fails the 4.5:1 body-text target. Supplied exact colors override these; never recolor assets or add spot colors.
motionAndInteraction: The dot grid stays fixed in spacing, angle, and local coordinates; animate content and masks instead. Movement should be smooth and authored where it helps, preserving deliberate cuts and reading holds, with no automatic springs or bounce. Video runs on seekable composition time, and scroll interaction is optional. Motion-012 and motion-015 are optional candidates, usable only when the scene supports them.
audio: The style specifies no audio. No fixed genre, tempo, voice, or mandatory layer is assigned. Choose music, voiceover, effects, ambience, or silence based on topic, audience, and motion. Honor supplied requirements and authorized assets, and verify speech clarity, balance, absence of clipping, and picture sync.
assetRequirements: Task-specific assets are unspecified; source artwork is needed for luminance separations, along with any copy, fonts, and timing. Load local fonts and assets before rendering. Optional preprocessing may use Pillow in Python or Sharp in Node.js. Duration, aspect ratio, resolution, and frame rate are unspecified, and examples are not requirements. Report any missing assets.
combinations: Halftone alone suits tonal content. Style-019 adds an editorial grid and type hierarchy; text stays unhalftoned and red appears at most once per view. Style-060 adds toon-lit 3D forms that drive the dots, avoiding glossy reflections. Hybrids must keep dots anchored. Omit chapters for very short topics or when transitions obscure causality.
productionApproach: HyperFrames is the primary pipeline for composition, timing, audio sync, validation, and export, using a paused GSAP timeline registered per composition. Remotion is a fallback only when HyperFrames is unavailable or a verified limit applies, and the reason must be recorded. Canvas 2D or a luminance halftone shader renders the dots. Check key frames, watch the full video, then deliver the project, contact sheet, parameters, and render instructions.
